title: Swap and pop
description:
`erase` in the middle of a vector slides every later element down by one. For a big vector that is a lot of copying, and often the order does not matter at all (a list of live particles, enemies, open connections).

When order does not matter there is a constant-time way: overwrite the doomed element with the **last** one, then `pop_back`.

Rewrite `removeUnordered` that way.
hints: Take care when `index` is already the last element: moving an object onto itself is not something to rely on.
rules: Do not call `erase`; move the last element into the gap and `pop_back`.

rules.message: Do not call `erase`; move the last element into the gap and `pop_back`.
